subject.title: [Reliability]: Enforce atomic intent→execution flow to prevent orphan pre-action notices

question: Should OpenClaw add a public agent-run transaction lifecycle now, and should it be standalone or folded into structured process events?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix defines new public lifecycle semantics across protocol, runtime, sessions, clients, and possibly policy behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the durable contract shape.

options.title: Design Additive Transaction Contract
options.body: Define run.begin, execution evidence, run.commit/run.abort, structured blocker payloads, compatibility behavior, and tests as a core protocol/runtime contract.

options.title: Fold Into Process Events
options.body: Make this issue's commit/abort guarantees acceptance criteria for the broader structured process-event work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52826.

options.title: Keep Existing Safeguards Only
options.body: Treat strict-agentic and incomplete-turn handling as sufficient for now, then narrow this issue to docs or telemetry instead of a new contract.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Transaction Contract
recommendation.body: Define run.begin, execution evidence, run.commit/run.abort, structured blocker payloads, compatibility behavior, and tests as a core protocol/runtime contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the prior keep-open product-contract review and has the strongest adjacent terminal-outcome and agent.wait history.
